diagnostic_evidence.quote: which only uses 50 parallel preconditioned Jacobi iterations.

issues.failure_explanation: The paper claims that any finite number of preconditioned iterations, with no error control, still guarantees global convergence. Every convergence proof instead relies on the exact first-order optimality condition for y^n. No inexact-oracle, perturbation, or error-control argument is supplied, so the advertised guarantee is unsupported.

failure_location.quote: It is important to note that we will prove that any finite and feasible preconditioned iterations can ensure the global convergence of the whole nonlinear second-order convex splitting method.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Either add an inexact-oracle analysis showing sufficient decrease and KL properties under bounded subproblem error, or restrict the claims to exact subproblem solves.
issues.overall_effect: The abstract and preliminary claims overstate the scope; the numerical experiments that stop the subproblem solver after a fixed number of preconditioned iterations are not covered by the convergence theory.
issues.title: Unsupported claim that finitely many preconditioned iterations without error control preserve global convergence
issues.why_classification: A supported resolution requires a new inexact-oracle proof architecture; the advertised finite-iteration guarantee is not a minor repair.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: otherwise, we terminate the line search and set $\lambda_n=0$

issues.failure_explanation: Step 6 of Algorithm alg:cap backtracks lambda by beta but has no stopping rule if no positive lambda satisfies the Armijo inequality. For the extrapolated case hat u = tilde u, d^n need not be a descent direction, so the loop can run forever. The lambda=0 fallback introduced later in eq:line:search:til is not part of the algorithm.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Add a termination rule to Step 6, e.g., if lambda falls below a prescribed tolerance, set lambda=0.
issues.overall_effect: The algorithm is not well-defined for the tilde u case, and Theorems thm:square:sum:til and thm:globalconverg:M assume a fallback that the algorithm does not implement.
issues.title: Algorithm line search has no termination rule when no positive step satisfies Armijo
issues.why_classification: A contained algorithmic fix restores well-definedness and aligns the algorithm with the later line-search rule, without changing the mathematical framework.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: With the energy $E(x)$ being level-bounded on $x$, it can be checked that $A(x,y)$ is thus level-bounded on $(x,y)$.

issues.failure_explanation: The theorems conclude that A (or tilde A) has a finite limit and that u^n is bounded, but the proof uses level-boundedness of E, which is not among the stated assumptions. Without it, the monotone sequence may be unbounded below and the summability bound is unjustified.

failure_location.quote: Assuming $h(u)$ and $f(u)$ are Lipschitz continuous, $A(x,y) = E(x) + (\frac{L}{2}+\frac{1}{3\delta t})\|x-y\|^2$ is a KL function and  $0\le\lambda_n< \lambda_{\max} =\sqrt{\frac{4}{3\delta tL} - \frac12}-1$.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Add level-boundedness (or boundedness below) of E to the hypotheses of the three theorems.
issues.overall_effect: The limit, boundedness, and summability conclusions of thm:globalconverg, thm:square:sum:til, and thm:globalconverg:M are unsupported as stated.
issues.title: Convergence theorems omit the level-boundedness hypothesis needed for the monotone limit
issues.why_classification: Adding a standard level-boundedness condition preserves all conclusions and the proof already uses it.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: \|u^{n+2}-u^{n+1}\|^2\leq \Tilde{C}(\|u^{n+2} - u^{n+1}\| + \|u^{n+1} - u^{n}\|)\Psi(u^n, u^{n+1}, u^{n+2}, \zeta), where $\tilde{C} = \frac{\alpha\lambda_{\min} + c(\lambda_{\max}, \delta t, L)}{(1+\lambda_{\max})^2}$.

issues.failure_explanation: The proof derives an algebraically false identity for f(u^{n+1}) from eq:solve:y:pre:general; the correct identity contains one-half factors and +1/2 f(u^n). Later it sets tilde C to the reciprocal of the constant that should multiply Psi, dropping C_L. The displayed inequalities are invalid as written, though the conclusions can be repaired with the correct identity and a redefined constant.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the false identity with the correct update equation and redefine tilde C to include C_L.
issues.overall_effect: The proof of thm:globalconverg contains invalid inference steps; the theorem's conclusions remain true after local repair.
issues.title: Invalid algebraic steps in the proof of thm:globalconverg
issues.why_classification: Both errors are local algebraic mistakes; the stated conclusions survive with a short correction.

issues.failure_explanation: Statement (iii) gives the rate n^{-(1-theta)/(2theta-2)}. Since 2theta-2<0 for theta<1, this is n^{1/2}, a growing and trivial bound. The appendix proof derives the correct exponent rho=(1-theta)/(2theta-1).
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Change the denominator in statement (iii) from 2theta-2 to 2theta-1.
issues.overall_effect: The advertised local convergence rate for theta in (1/2,1) is false as stated; the correct rate appears only in the appendix proof.
issues.title: Local rate theorem states a trivial exponent for theta in (1/2,1)
issues.why_classification: The correction is a one-symbol repair that restores the rate already proved in the appendix, with no loss of content.

issues.failure_explanation: Substituting hat u^n = tilde u^n into eq:solve:y:pre:general gives M(y^n-tilde u^n), not (2M/delta t)(y^n-tilde u^n). issues.failure_explanation: The displayed splitting eq:another:split places mu*tilde P(u) in the concave part, but eq:lsp defines the objective with -tilde P(u). Expanding the split gives mu H_alpha + 1/2||Au-b||^2 - mu*tilde P, which is not the objective of eq:lsp unless mu=1.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace mu*tilde P by tilde P in eq:another:split and regenerate the BDCA results.
issues.overall_effect: The BDCA comparison is performed on a different objective, so the numerical comparison with BapDCA_ls-t is unreliable.
issues.title: BDCA splitting uses mu*tilde P instead of tilde P, changing the objective
issues.why_classification: The repair is a one-term correction, but it changes the comparison algorithm and requires new numerical results.

issues.failure_explanation: The prior term is eta/2 sum Lambda(i)(u(i)-y(i))^2 with Lambda(i)=2y(i)-1. For y(i)=0, Lambda(i)=-1, making the term -eta/2 u(i)^2, which is concave. Thus H is not convex, violating a core assumption of the method.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Use nonnegative prior weights or restrict the label set; this changes the model or the experiment.
issues.overall_effect: The Ginzburg-Landau numerical example does not satisfy the convexity assumption required by the convergence theory.
issues.title: Ginzburg-Landau prior term can make H nonconvex
issues.why_classification: The defect is concrete and requires modifying the model or the experiment, but it does not affect the general convergence theory.

issues.failure_explanation: F(u)=1/epsilon W(u) with W(u)=1/4 sum (u_i^2-1)^2 has gradient component (1/epsilon) u_i(u_i^2-1), whose derivative (1/epsilon)(3u_i^2-1) is unbounded. Hence grad F is not globally Lipschitz, contradicting the standing assumption that grad F has a Lipschitz constant L.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Restrict to a bounded domain or iterate set and add a local Lipschitz analysis, or modify the model.
issues.overall_effect: The convergence theory does not apply to the Ginzburg-Landau model as stated.
issues.title: Ginzburg-Landau double-well gradient is not globally Lipschitz
issues.why_classification: The violation is clear and requires a new boundedness argument or model change, but it is confined to one numerical example.

issues.failure_explanation: The displayed splitting expands to graph plus prior minus (1/epsilon)W, while the original functional eq:nonlocalGL has plus (1/epsilon)W. The sign of the double-well term is wrong, so the other algorithms solve a different functional.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Correct the sign in the concave part and rerun the comparison algorithms.
issues.overall_effect: The DCA, pDCA_e, BDCA, and BaDCA_ls comparison in Table tab:nonlocalGLmodel is invalid.
issues.title: Ginzburg-Landau comparison splitting has the wrong sign for the double-well term
issues.why_classification: The error is a clear sign mistake, but fixing it changes the comparison experiments and requires new numerical results.

issues.failure_explanation: Proposition prop:proximal_to_pre requires h(u)=Au-b_0. For the SCAD problem, H(u)=mu H_alpha(u)+1/2||Au-b||^2, so h(u)=mu grad H_alpha(u)+A^T(Au-b) is nonlinear. The paper's use of preconditioned Jacobi iterations for BapDCA is therefore not justified by the stated preconditioned iteration.
